tb21_profile.skill: Compose a correct qemu-system command line (snapshot mode, VNC display, monitor socket, headless) and leave the VM plus its access path running as background services, then verify the guest reached its desktop
tb21_profile.domain: Linux virtualization sysadmin — QEMU/KVM, VNC displays and port arithmetic, QEMU monitor/QMP over a unix socket, nginx fronting on port 80, daemonised processes
tb21_profile.task_form: configure-a-service: multi-component infrastructure brought up to a written spec and left running, verified by probing the live system

searches: tools.py search tmax "qemu-system|-vnc|VNC display|snapshot mode|monitor socket|hostfwd" -n 25

notes: TMax is exceptionally strong here: it contains roughly thirty tasks that literally compose qemu-system command lines with -vnc, -nographic, -daemonize, PID files, QMP/monitor sockets and hostfwd, so eight of the top ten are TMax and the top four are near-exact. TerminalWorld contributes genuine KVM/libvirt/cloud-image work. The two SWE corpora have no virtualization at all — SWE-Smith matched zero documents for qemu/VNC/libvirt/KVM and SWE-Rebench only two, so both lists are honest but weak (mostly 2s and 3s) and rest on adjacent skills: bind-address parsing, unix-socket lifecycle, daemon startup, reverse-proxy headers, VM guest agents. Retrieval trap worth flagging: pyupio__safety pr_508 ranked top of the SWE-Smith shortlist purely because it says 'headless', and it is about CLI auth — excluded.
